questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose this destination primarily because of the opportunity to study at the University of California system and experience academic life in the United States. The location of the university was also an important factor. Santa Cruz offers a unique campus environment with nature, ocean views, and a relaxed atmosphere that differs significantly from most European universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Another important aspect was the possibility to take interesting courses within computer science while also having some flexibility in course selection. Additionally, being close to Silicon Valley made the destination attractive from an academic and professional perspective.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. U get all the help u need.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had transportation to campus residence. Free food first days. Help registering for events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Orientation upon arrival first quarter was fantastic. BUT if u stay for two quarters, then when coming back for second quarter, there is no introduction to new student arrivals.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a apartment in the college: International Community Center, where 50% were exchange students (at UCSC).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Students could either buy a campus meal plan and eat at dining halls or cook themselves. In the apartments there was a shared kitchen, so it was possible to cook your own meals.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus makes it very easy to meet other students and participate in campus activities. However, the campus is large, so getting around can take some time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was done online through the university system. Some courses required permission or waitlisting, so it sometimes took a bit of time to finalize the schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office and academic advisors were available to help with course registration and general questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all of the classes I wanted, although some required waitlisting before getting a spot. Exchange students basically get access to all they want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have backup courses prepared, as some classes can fill up quickly. It is also useful to join waitlists early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easy, easy and easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much better. Evaluation throughout the course with quizzes, midterms, attendance...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Programming, Parallel & Concurrent Programming,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pick the easiest.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some additional costs included campus fees, transportation for trips outside Santa Cruz, and higher prices for groceries and eating out compared to Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dining hall was quite expensive, so i ate two times a day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many student clubs, sports activities, social events, and cultural organizations. The university also organized events for international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining student clubs and outdoor activities like hiking or surfing. It is a good way to meet people and experience the local environment.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit Santa Cruz beaches, explore San Francisco, and take trips along the California coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy since the environment is very international and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, attend campus events, and talk to classmates in group projects.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The academic system with continuous assignments and participation was slightly different from what I was used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open and relaxed atmosphere, the international environment, and the strong outdoor culture around the university.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be ready to engang and talk to people, its so easy and part of the culture in CA. 

Take advantage of the outdoor activities and travel opportunities.

Join clubs or student events to meet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The campus is large and surrounded by nature, so be prepared to walk a lot and plan time to get between classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from many different countries and experiencing life and studying in California.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the faster quarter system and the continuous workload during the term.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I can really recommend choosing University of California, Santa Cruz. You are in central CA, and can go both north to SF and other campus (Stanford, UCSB), and u can go south to UCSB, UCLA, UCSD. 

Also, the distance to different national parks is shorter, such as Yosemite, Joshua Tree, Sequoia Tree, etc... Only downside about UCSC is that it is extremely expensive but will all you get for the money, IT IS MORE THAN WORTH IT!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
